plan: Reduce QQQI to 20% to lower concentration.

conservative.read: This plan aims for capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged ETFs and exiting weak positions, holding a larger cash buffer implicitly. Drawdowns should be limited.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to manage concentration.
Reduce exposure in weaker AI/Software (METU, PLTU) and Semiconductor (MUU) names.
Maintain small positions in leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) at 2% and 1% respectively.
Trim MSFU slightly to 2% while still positive.
Buy Apple (AAPL) at 4% for balanced growth.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% monthly return by reducing leverage and concentration while adding a quality name. It aims for risk-first growth, keeping a moderate cash buffer. Drawdowns are expected to be manageable.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to manage concentration.
Reduce CRWD to 6% to free up capital.
Sell broad index ETFs (SPY, QQQ) to concentrate.
Exit weak Semiconductor (SMH) and AI/Software (METU) positions.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly return by concentrating in high-conviction names and increasing leveraged ETF exposure. It accepts higher risk, including larger potential drawdowns and the daily rebalancing decay of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% for enhanced income.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to minimize risk.
Exit speculative AI/Software (METU, MSFU, PLTU) and Semiconductor (MUU) positions.
Add SPY to 10% for broad market exposure and stability.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income.

income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly return through distributions from QQQI and SPY, while cutting all speculative and leveraged positions. It prioritizes capital preservation and consistent income over growth. NAV can still decline in market downturns.
